title: Direct conversion of human keratinocytic cells towards a melanocyte-like phenotype
protocol: Prewarm DMEM without supplements and x-tremeGENE9 DNA transfection reagent to room temperature.
Pipette 770 μl of DMEM without supplements into a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Add 50 µl of x-tremeGENE9 DNA transfection reagent directly to the DMEM.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Mix transfer plasmid containing your gene of interest, packaging plasmid pCMV-dR8.91, and envelope plasmid pCMV-VSV-G in specific ratios before adding them to the DMEM/x-tremeGENE9 mix.
Check the correct identity of your plasmid on a regular basis with restriction digestion and sequencing.
Determine the concentration of plasmid before using it for transfection.
Allow new DNA preparations to dissolve in water or buffer overnight at 4°C.
Estimate the concentration from samples loaded on agarose gels by comparing band intensity with the ladder.
Incubate at RT for 30 minutes.
Aspirate the old medium from T75 flask of HEK293T cells.
Add new MEF medium to the T75 flask.
Check HEK cells for mycoplasma contamination before use.
Add the DMEM/x-tremeGENE/DNA mix dropwise to the medium of the HEK cultures.
Discard the medium after 24 hours.
Add fresh MEF medium to the HEK cultures.
Harvest the supernatant after 12 hours.
Store the harvested supernatant at 4°C.
Harvest the supernatant again after another 12 and 24 hours on day 3.
Filter the pooled supernatants through a 0.45-µm PVDF filter to remove cells.
Store filtered supernatants for up to 2-4 weeks at 4°C.
Aliquot the filtered supernatant and store it at -80°C for long-term storage.
Alternatively, centrifuge the supernatant with an ultracentrifuge to concentrate the virus.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 20,000 g and 4°C for 2 hours on day 4.
Completely remove the liquid from the supernatant.
Add 100 µl of PBS to the pellet.
Aliquot the resuspended virus and store it at -80°C for long-term storage.
Avoid repeated freeze- and thaw-cycles of aliquots.
Prewarm T/E solution to room temperature.
Aspirate the medium and wash the cells once with PBS.
Add T/E to the cells and incubate at 37°C until all cells are detached from the surface.
Add medium and carefully rinse the cells off the surface. Transfer the cells into a 15ml conical test tube and spin them down at 1200 rpm for 5 min. Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in a small volume of medium.
Add the same amount of freezing medium and mix carefully.
Aliquot the cell suspension at 1 ml each into cryotubes.
Put the cryotubes into a freezing container and leave them at 4°C for about 2 h.
Put the freezing container at -80°C over night.
For long-term storage transfer the cells into a liquid nitrogen tank.
Seed keratinocytic cells, such as HaCaT or MET-4 cells, in a 6-well plate so that they are approximately 20% confluent the day after.
Add 2 ml of fresh MEF medium to each well for HaCaT cells, or DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin for MET-4 cells.
Add 500 µl of supernatant containing viral particles or 3 µl of concentrated solution of viral particles to each well.
Incubate the cells with the virus overnight.
Replace the medium containing viral particles with fresh growth medium.
Let the cells grow for at least 24 hours before starting the selection process.
Wash the cells four times with PBS to remove any residual virus particles.
Add fresh MEF medium (HaCaT) or basic DMEM (MET-4) to infected cells.
Include puromycin at a final concentration of 0.2 µg/ml in the medium.
Include zeocin at a final concentration of 50 µg/ml in the medium.
Add puromycin at the same concentration to non-infected control wells.
Add zeocin at the same concentration to another well with non-infected cells.
Expose cells to increasing concentrations of antibiotics to determine optimal concentration.
Start selection process when cell density does not exceed 50% confluence.
Passage too confluent cells before starting the selection process.
Replace medium with fresh antibiotic-containing medium every two days.
Consider the minimal concentration that kills all cells within one week as optimal.
Add fresh growth medium with puromycin and zeocin every other day until all uninfected control cells are dead.
Propagate the selected cells and plate them for superinfection with the transdifferentiation factor cocktail.
Freeze some aliquots of infected cells as a backup.
Plate keratinocytic cells such as HaCaT or MET-4 cells, infected with and selected for the MITF reporter construct and rtTA, to reach 30-50% confluence the following day.
Add 2 ml of fresh MEF medium (HaCaT) or basic DMEM (MET-4) to each well.
Add 3 µl of each concentrated virus to the wells.
Incubate cells with viral particles overnight.
Wash the cells four times with PBS to remove any residual virus particles.
Add 2 ml of MEF medium (for HaCaT cells) or basic DMEM (for MET-4 cells) containing doxycycline at a final concentration of 1 µg/ml to the cells.
Change the medium every two to three days.
Switch to MCDB medium with 1 µg/ml doxycycline one week after induction and continue changing the medium every two to three days.
Withdraw doxycycline from the medium two weeks after induction.
Continue cultivating the cells in MCDB medium.
Prewarm T/E solution to room temperature.
Aspirate the MCDB medium and wash the cells once with PBS.
Add T/E to the cells and incubate for two minutes at 37°C.
Add MCDB medium and carefully rinse the cells off the surface.
Transfer the cells into a fresh cell culture flask.
Let the cells grow to confluence and repeat steps until pure fractions of spindle-shaped cells are obtained.
Prewarm T/E solution to room temperature.
Aspirate the MCDB medium and wash the cells once with PBS.
Add T/E to the cells and incubate for two minutes at 37°C.
Add MCDB medium and carefully rinse the cells off the surface.
Spin down the cells at 1200 rpm (when using conical test tubes) or 4000 rpm (when using microcentrifuge tubes) for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Purify total RNA from the cells with the RNeasy Mini Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Determine concentration and purity of your RNA samples with a NanoDrop.
Synthesize first-strand cDNA using the RevertAid First Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit.
Aspirate the MCDB medium from cells.
Add PBS to the cells.
Scratch the cells off the surface with a cell scraper and transfer them into a 15ml conical test tube or microcentrifuge tube.
Spin down the cells at 1200 rpm (conical tubes) or 4000 rpm (microcentrifuge tubes).
Discard the supernatant.
Lyse the cells by resuspending them in RIPA buffer and incubate for 10 min at 4°C on a rotating wheel.
Spin down all cell debris at 15,000 g and 4°C for 10 min.
Transfer the aqueous solution into a new prechilled microcentrifuge tube.
Store the supernatant at -80°C if necessary.
Determine the protein concentration of each sample using the Pierce BCA Protein Assay kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Use the protein lysate for Western blot analysis.
Load 20-50 μg per sample on a gel.
